supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: recommendationservice_latency-90 z=173.44 (867.2%); recommendationservice_latency-50 z=155.9 (779.5%); recommendationservice_cpu z=67.44 (655.6%); frontend_latency-50 z=5.89 (29.5%)
traces for recommendationservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 1.04->2.57ms (2.48x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 3.88->5.43ms (1.4x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: An injected network or sleep delay would not raise CPU 655% (z=67.44); CPU rising together with latency points to CPU saturation (E1).

Frontend latency-50 deviation is small (29.5%, z=5.89) next to recommendationservice's 779-867% (E1). Recommendationservice's own self-time rose 2.48x and caller-observed (inbound) self-time also rose, so the slowdown starts in recommendationservice (E2).

proposed_fix.description: Find and stop the CPU-hogging process in the recommendationservice pod, or restart or scale out the pod. Raise the CPU limit or add replicas until latency returns to baseline.

investigation.thought: No evidence yet, so start with an unfiltered metric query that ranks every service and metric by before/after-alert deviation.
